title: Guardrails

chain.title: How settings are inherited
chain.hint: Every part is inherited on its own. A request takes each part from the most specific level that sets it: its API key, then its project, department, and company. Parts that no level sets come from the platform policy.

overrides.title: Overrides
overrides.hint: Companies, departments, projects, and API keys that set parts themselves. Inherited parts follow the level above.
overrides.emptyHint: Every request follows the platform policy. Add an override to give a company, department, project, or API key its own settings for any part.
overrides.removeConfirmHint: Every part then follows the level above again.

inspector.empty: Pick a target to see its effective policy.

pii.title: Platform policy for personal data
pii.hint: Applies to every request unless its API key, project, department, or company sets personal data itself.

enableHint: Applies to text in chat, completions, messages, responses, batches, embeddings, moderations, image prompts, speech input, and the playground. Uploaded files and audio are not scanned.
modeHint: Block rejects the request with 400 pii_blocked before it reaches the model. Mask keeps placeholders in the response and in logs. Restore sends numbered placeholders to the model, then puts the original personal values back in the client response. It also adds a short system instruction that tells the model to work with each placeholder as if it were the real value. Logs stay masked. Secrets, keys, and tokens are never restored.
outputHint: New personal data in the model output is masked before the client sees it. In restore mode, values from the prompt are put back after that check.
detectorOption: {detector, select, patterns {Patterns} model {Redaction model} both {Model and patterns} other {{detector}}}
detectorHint: {detector, select, patterns {Fixed rules find structured values such as email addresses, card numbers, and IDs.} model {The redaction model finds names, addresses, and other personal data in free text. Secrets and credentials are always caught by patterns first.} both {The redaction model and the patterns both run, and overlapping matches count once. Secrets and credentials are always caught by patterns first.} other {}}
failureOption: {failure, select, patterns {Fall back to patterns} block {Block the request (503)} other {{failure}}}
failureHint: Fallback redacts with patterns and logs a warning without request content. Block rejects the request with 503 pii_detector_unavailable.

model.title: Redaction model
model.description: Used by every policy whose detection includes the model, overrides included. Secrets never reach it.

model.hint: {configured, select, true {LLMHUB_REDACTOR_URL provides the pii-tracer alias.} other {Pick an internal alias that speaks the token classification protocol, or set LLMHUB_REDACTOR_URL.}}
model.timeoutHint: Per request. When it runs out, the failure setting applies.
model.language: PII-Tracer documents English. Its model card does not state German coverage, so test German samples here before you rely on it, and prefer Model and patterns for structured IDs.
model.testerHint: Sends the sample to the selected model and lists the spans it finds. Nothing is stored.

injection.hint: Heuristics for common injection phrases in English and German, checked in user and tool content. System and developer instructions are not checked.

content.logsHint: Request logs list every match in prompts and responses. A blocked response ends with finish reason content_filter (stop reason refusal on Messages), and stored log content keeps masked text masked.
content.streamHint: Streams are checked chunk by chunk with a short look-back. A blocked stream stops at the match, so text sent before it has already reached the client. Masking only covers matches within one chunk.
